Mo’unga to start as All Blacks name side for final South Africa Test
item.description: Richie Mo’unga will start at flyhalf as the All Blacks take on South Africa in the fourth and final Test of their series in Baltimore this weekend. Codie Taylor will captain the side at hooker and will team up with Ethan De Groot and Fletcher Newell in the front row.
item.content:encoded:
Richie Mo’unga will start at flyhalf as the All Blacks take on South Africa in the fourth and final Test of their series in Baltimore this weekend.

Codie Taylor will captain the side at hooker and will team up with Ethan De Groot and Fletcher Newell in the front row.

Patrick Tuipulotu and Sam Darry start at lock, while Tupou Vaa’i, Ethan Blackadder and Peter Lakai complete the forward pack.

Cam Roigard will partner with Mo’unga at the halves while Jordie Barrett and Anton Lienert-Brown will combine in the midfields.

Josh Moorby, Will Jordan and Damian McKenzie make up the back three.

Beauden Barrett, Rieko Ioane and Wallace Sititi are among the players named on the bench.

The All Blacks will face South Africa at M&T Bank Stadium in Baltimore, with the match kicking off at 9am this Sunday.

item.title: Ikanivere to lead ?Flying Fijians for Canada clash
item.description: The starting XV features a mix of experienced campaigners and emerging talent, with Peni Ravai named at loosehead prop and Mesake Doge at tight-head prop alongside Ikanivere in the front row. Mesake Vocevoce and Temo Mayanavanua are named in the second row, providing Fiji with size and power in the forward pack.
item.content:encoded:
The starting XV features a mix of experienced campaigners and emerging talent, with Peni Ravai named at loosehead prop and Mesake Doge at tight-head prop alongside Ikanivere in the front row.

Mesake Vocevoce and Temo Mayanavanua are named in the second row, providing Fiji with size and power in the forward pack.

In the loose forwards, Kitione Salawa , Motikiai Murray and Isoa Tuwai will look to provide Fiji with physicality at the breakdown and strong ball-carrying options.

The halfback pairing sees Frank Lomani take charge at scrum-half, while the backline also includes Isaia Armstrong-Ravula at fly-half.

Manasa Mataele is named on the wing, with Kalaveti Ravouvou and Virimi Vakatawa at inside and outside centre.

Jone Nasova is named on the blindside wing, while Sireli Rabitu is at full back.

The Flying Fijians have also named a strong bench, with players including Peniasi Cakobau and Meli Tuni, Inoke Ravuiwasa, Isoa Nasilasila, Joseva Tamani covering the forwards while and Terio Tamani, Caleb Muntz and Tuidraki Samusamuvodre on the bench for the backs.

The match will be played at Hanazono Rugby Stadium , with kick-off scheduled for 7pm this Saturday .

item.title: Nasinu faces tough BOG semi-final test against Rewa
item.description: Nasinu FC will be aiming to reach the Extra Battle of the Giants final for the first time since 2019 when it faces nine-time champions Stratum/PPCL Rewa FC in the second semi-final this Saturday. The Giant Killers bounced back from an opening 1-0 loss to Extra Supermarket Labasa FC, beat ing Blue Gas Navua FC 1-nil and Global Care Suva FC 2-1 to secure their place in the last four.
item.content:encoded:
Nasinu FC will be aiming to reach the Extra Battle of the Giants final for the first time since 2019 when it faces nine-time champions Stratum/PPCL Rewa FC in the second semi-final this Saturday.

The Giant Killers bounced back from an opening 1-0 loss to Extra Supermarket Labasa FC, beat ing Blue Gas Navua FC 1-nil and Global Care Suva FC 2-1 to secure their place in the last four.

Rewa topped Group B with six points after beating Khelvin Engineering Lautoka FC 2-0, and Dayal’s Steel Ba FC 3-0 .

The Delta Tigers will enter the semi-final with plenty of experience, with several players having featured in the OFC Men’s Champions League earlier this season.

Nasinu will be determined to continue its impressive run and cause another upset when the two sides meet at 4.30pm this Saturday at 4R Stadium, Govind Park, Ba.

Meanwhile, Ba will face Suva in the first semi-final at 2pm.

The final is scheduled for 3pm on Sunday.
